title: Negotiation protocol for cross-runtime trace compatibility in SDKs
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: Different runtimes and SDK versions used by Redwood customers (edge SDKs, server-side agents, and worker pools) put trace context into headers or sidebands in slightly incompatible ways (different header names, timestamp encodings, optional baggage fields). This leads to broken end-to-end traces, high tail latency on trace reconstruction, and noisy sampling mismatches in dashboards.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight negotiation protocol that runs at SDK initialization and first request handshake to agree on a mutually compatible trace-carryforward format. The protocol should: (1) be backwards-compatible with existing clients that do not speak the negotiation layer; (2) add minimal bytes to requests; (3) allow feature flags (e.g., full-baggage, compressed-kv, monotonic-span-ids); (4) fallback deterministically to a safe legacy envelope when negotiation fails; (5) provide observability signals (negotiation success/failure, chosen semantic version) for rollout and metrics.

Success metrics: increase end-to-end trace stitch rate from 93% to >= 99% for multi-runtime flows; reduce trace reconstruction CPU consumption in trace-processor by 30% for negotiated flows; zero customer-visible errors during canary rollout.

Scope: implement SDK-side negotiation in Node/Go/Java SDKs, add server-side acceptor in proxy/edge (ingress), and a runtime flag in the inference runtime to enable preferred formats. Do not change persisted trace storage model (trace-processor will map format to internal shape).

Design summary: negotiation runs as an optional, idempotent exchange piggybacked on the first API request header. Client adds single header X-RI-TNP: v1;cap=basic,cflags=compact-baggage;nonce=hex. Server responds with X-RI-TNP-ACK: v1;agreed=basic;cflags=compact-baggage;nonce=hex;sig=short. If both sides support 'v2' features, they may upgrade after explicit acknowledgement. For clients that don't send TNP header, the server uses a header-inferencing stage and marks the exchange as legacy. The negotiation payload is intentionally human-readable key=value pairs to simplify debugging and avoid complex binary parsing in early rollout.

Compatibility rules and fallbacks: when headers mismatch or ACK absent, server falls back to legacy-compat envelope and emits metric ri.tnp.negotiation.failure_reason with tags. Negotiation is purely an optimization and must not change request routing.

Testing and rollout plan: unit tests for header parsing, fuzz tests for malformed headers, interop matrix tests across Node/Go/Java SDK versions in CI. Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with detailed dashboards: negotiation success rate, negotiation latency histogram, fraction of traces stitched via negotiated path, and errors by SDK version.

Open decisions: whether to include a short integrity signature in v1 (we implement a short HMAC with per-customer key in a later phase) and exact semantic version bytes for v2.

Non-goals: This ticket does not add new persistent storage formats or change sampling policy logic (those will be separate follow-ups).

Implementation notes: prefer a minimal parsing implementation in SDKs to avoid extra allocations; negotiation header parsing should be lazy and cached per process. Add feature gate in runtime-1.22 to accept TNP and emit new metrics.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Gomez: Created initial ticket after a postmortem where 7 customer traces were irrecoverable due to a header naming mismatch between old Java agent and new edge proxy. Included initial protocol sketch.

2025-02-19 - Marco Liu: Implemented PoC parser in Node SDK and a toy acceptor in the edge proxy. Observed negotiation adds ~40 bytes to request headers and ~0.4ms median processing on ingress in microbenchmarks.

2025-02-21 - Priya Nair (Observability): Reviewed design. Requested metric tags for sdk_version and client_region, and asked that all negotiation failures include failure_reason tag for alerting. Marked security_review_required for HMAC plan.

2025-02-23 - Marco Liu: Added CI interop matrix with Docker images for node:14/18, go1.20, java17. Early tests show go SDK emits legacy header name by default; plan added to patch Go SDK to emit negotiation header behind feature flag.

2025-02-25 - Design review: Carlos Mendes (Design): Suggested human-readable header for easier debugging, and recommended consistent field order in header to make diffs reliable for logs. Approved UX for error surface in Console rollout dashboard.
2025-02-25 - Next steps: finalize header spec doc, add implementation tickets for Node/Go/Java, open PR to edge proxy, instrument runtime metric gate, and prepare canary dashboard.
